decision.question: review size
decision.why: role reshape: singleton, renew on wake, feedback inbox, role-spend

findings.text: `review/diff.patch` was empty (0 bytes); I reviewed `git diff michael/dev...HEAD` instead. Regenerate the patch so the record matches what landed.

Servex/agents/Agents.js:677-684 (`wake`): when the singleton is live and dormant, `this.spawn` hits the singleton branch (Agents.js:134-136) and sends the renewal text to the live agent, then `awaken` may renew again, so a `renew` event can be emitted twice and the renewal prompt delivered alongside the waking message. Harmless in practice, but worth a test for "live dormant + due" in singleton.test.mjs.

Servex/agents/ModuleInbox.js:`wake_for` only wakes when `row.fix` is set, so `obvious: true` with no `fix` never wakes the mastermind. The tool text says "obvious ... wakes at once"; either require `fix` in the description or drop the `fix` gate for `obvious`.
Server/role-spend.mjs:`main` detection builds a path from `import.meta.url.pathname` with a Windows drive regex; it works on this machine but `fileURLToPath` would be simpler and safer.

Requirements 1-6 are met in code: rename plus pointer at servex-mastermind.md, `singleton` + `renew` on the roles.js row, `Respawn.AGENTS` emptied, `module_inbox` extended with `fix`/`repeat_of`/`obvious` and the third-repeat wake, spend script, and the generic `mastermind` row now loading its own readme. I did not re-run the tests; the 23-check singleton test is claimed in requirements.md.

answer.reply: noted: the reviewer read the branch diff; the patch file is regenerated by the next review run.
fixed: wake() renews only a stopped or registry-only agent; a live dormant one renews in awaken(), so one renew per wake.
fixed: the obvious flag description says to give a fix; a line with no fix is an ask and wakes nobody (kept on purpose).
fixed: role-spend.mjs uses fileURLToPath for its main check.
noted: tests re-run after the fixes, singleton 23 passing.
fixed: the role is never compacted (compact_after null) and its token line is 100k, so an idle session past 100k sleeps and the next wake is a fresh session.
fixed: the predecessor, VS Code tab and where-you-write sections are rewritten for the one-id model.
fixed: it wakes on exactly the third repeat, and again only when a problem comes back after an outcome line (the fix did not hold); tested.
noted: a spawn is an explicit request, so it starts the one session even after a stop; a message (send) still goes through the revive guard.
noted: the readme stays where roles.js reads every role; its docs home is ai/.
noted: role-spend ALIASES lists old agent ids, which roles.js aliases (role words) do not cover.

findings.text: `compact_after: null` on the `ai-system-mastermind` row (`Servex/agents/roles.js:53`) also turns off the 400k safety ceiling, because `Agent.oversized()` returns null for any role with `compact_after === null` (`Servex/agents/Agents.js:1515`). That contradicts the row's own comment ("only the 400k safety ceiling applies mid-work"). Renewal only happens on a wake from dormant, so a session that keeps itself awake with timers (its readme's "Don't fall asleep with work in flight") is never renewed and never compacted, and it grows toward the 1M window. Fix: keep the ceiling for this role, e.g. `compact_after: { tokens: Infinity }` or an `oversized()` check that skips only nudges for `renew` roles, plus one test.

A singleton spawn looks only at `this.live` (`Agents.js:134`). After a Servex restart, a young session that exists only in the registry gets a brand-new session under the same id instead of being resumed, which loses its context for no reason. `Agents.wake()` already handles a registry-only agent; the singleton branch could route there when a registry row exists.

Changing the generic `mastermind` row's readme from `servex-mastermind` to `mastermind` (`roles.js:55`) changes the system prompt of every live Servex-spawned mastermind (e.g. a deputy) on its next resume. It is probably right, but nobody asked for it; it is recorded in requirements.md, so just check that the deputy's role still fits.

`Server/on-landing.mjs:23-24` still sends landing check failures to a `servex-mastermind` task folder, not to the new feedback inbox (`module_inbox`, module `ai`). The landing checks are the main source of "problem + fix" lines, so pointing them at the inbox would let the third-repeat wake actually fire.

`Server/role-spend.mjs` is good, simple code. Its `ALIASES` (line 31) is a second list of old ids next to `roles.js`. The second review accepted that; it is noted here only so the two get updated together.

answer.reply: fixed: the row no longer sets compact_after; a renew row skips only the nudge and the sleep compaction (Agent.nudge/sleep_compact), so the 400k ceiling still applies (tested).
fixed: a singleton found only in the registry is woken through wake(), which resumes it or renews it if due; the renewal spawn carries renewing so it cannot loop (tested).
fixed: on-landing.mjs sends those lines to module_inbox ai (no fix, so they wait for its next wake); the old servex-mastermind log no longer existed, so they were being dropped.
noted: ALIASES lists old agent ids, which roles.js role-word aliases do not cover; one place, beside the script that uses it.
